newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Airlines taps Pepsi exec as CFO.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Airlines taps Pepsi exec as CFO.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp reached outside the airline industry, tapping PepsiCo executive James Lawrence as its chief financial officer.
Lawrence fills a vacancy created by the resignation of Mickey Foret, who became president of Atlas Air Inc in May. The airline declined to comment on when Lawrence will assume the post.

"It's very exciting that they've filled this slot. They'll be going into labor negotiations, and they will need to have all their ducks in a row," said Helane Becker, an airline analyst with Smith Barney.
Lawrence's appointment continues Northwest's pattern of searching for talent beyond the airline industry, a strategy industry experts have applauded.
"The airline industry is not one of the best managed industries," Becker said.

"While airline expertise does help, Northwest has taken a lot (of employees) from outside. That way of thinking has clearly helped them. It's broadened their talent pool," said Glenn Engel, an analyst with Goldman Sachs.

Lawrence most recently served as president and chief executive of Pepsi-Cola Co Asia, Middle East, Africa. Before joining PepsiCo in 1992, Lawrence co-founded LEK Partnership, a management consulting firm specializing in corporate strategy, mergers and acquisitions.
Lawrence will now oversee Northwest's corporate finance and strategic planning activities, as well its fuel and aircraft purchasing subsidiaries, the airline said.
As part of his appointment at Northwest, Lawrence will immediately resign from the board of Trans World Airlines Inc, Northwest said.
Northwest's stock traded unchanged at 36-3/4 at 1555 EDT/1955 GMT.
